title: Your CRM Sync and AI Automation Hub

sections.label: 1 - CATCH THE CRM EVENT, PARK BAD DATA
sections.note: HubSpot is shown as the example CRM, any CRM swaps in at the first node and the write-back. Every event is mapped into one standard record, and anything missing or malformed waits in a review table with the exact field named.

sections.label: 2 - RUN EACH EVENT ONCE, ANSWER THE CRM FAST
sections.note: CRMs resend webhooks, so every event id is claimed once in a ledger and a repeat stops cold. The CRM gets its answer in milliseconds while the real work carries on behind it.

sections.label: 3 - CLAUDE SHAPES IT, EVERY SYSTEM GETS ITS COPY
sections.note: Claude cleans the names, maps the plan to invoice terms and writes the team summary, into a fixed schema. Ids and amounts come straight from the CRM, never from the model. A throttled call backs off and tries again.

sections.label: 4 - WRITE IT BACK TO THE CRM, CLOSE THE LOOP
sections.note: The rep sees the invoice number, ops record and sync time on the deal itself. The ledger row holds every id that was created, so any sync can be traced in one lookup.

sections.label: 5 - NOTHING FAILS QUIETLY
sections.note: One error trigger covers every step. The event is marked failed with its payload kept, and the team gets the deal, the step that broke and a link to the run, ready to replay.

nodes.label: 1 - HubSpot or Your CRM: Deal Moved to Closed Won
nodes.notes: HubSpot here as the example. Salesforce, Pipedrive, Zoho or GoHighLevel plug into this same spot.

nodes.label: 2 - Normalize and Validate Into One Standard Record
nodes.notes: CRM field names are mapped once, here. Required fields, email format, amount and currency are checked before anything moves.

nodes.label: 3 - Record Passes Validation?
3b - Park It in Needs Review With the Failing Field
nodes.notes: Bad data never reaches QuickBooks or the ops base. Someone fixes the field and replays it.

nodes.label: 4 - Sync Ledger: Claim This Event Id Once
nodes.notes: Unique key on the event id. A resent webhook inserts nothing, and the raw payload is kept for replay.

params.query:
INSERT INTO sync_ledger (event_id, crm, deal_id, execution_id, payload, status, claimed_at)
VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5::jsonb, 'claimed', now())
ON CONFLICT (event_id) DO NOTHING
RETURNING event_id, deal_id, true AS claimed;

nodes.label: 5 - Only New Events Continue
nodes.notes: A repeat delivery stops here, so no invoice or ops record is ever created twice.

nodes.label: 6 - Acknowledge the CRM Right Away
nodes.notes: Answer first, work after. A slow answer is what makes a CRM resend.

nodes.label: 7 - Claude Maps and Enriches the Record
nodes.notes: Judgment work only: clean names, read the plan terms, write the summary. Ids, emails and amounts pass straight through.

options.systemMessage: You turn one closed-won CRM deal into what each connected system needs. Clean the company name for display, read the plan text into a QuickBooks item and billing schedule, and write a two sentence summary for the team. Never invent or change an id, email or amount. If something needed is missing or unclear, set needs_review to true and name the field.

nodes.label: Claude
Target Schema: Ops Record, Invoice Terms, Team Summary

nodes.label: 8 - Airtable: Create the Ops Project Record
9 - QuickBooks: Create the First Invoice
nodes.notes: Line amount is the deal amount from the CRM divided by the installments. The model never sets a price.

nodes.label: 10 - QuickBooks Accepted It?
10b - Back Off 30 Seconds, Then Retry
nodes.notes: Rate limits and token refreshes are usually temporary, so it waits and tries again. Past the retry cap, the error path takes over.

nodes.label: 11 - Slack: Tell the Team the Deal Is Live

params.text: ={{ $('7 - Claude Maps and Enriches the Record').item.json.output.team_summary }}

nodes.label: 12 - HubSpot or Your CRM: Write Ids and Sync Status to the Deal
nodes.notes: Only the sync fields are written, so the write-back can never retrigger this workflow.

params.url: =https://api.hubapi.com/crm/v3/objects/deals/{{ $('2 - Normalize and Validate Into One Standard Record').item.json.deal.deal_id }}

nodes.label: 13 - Sync Ledger: Mark Done With Every Id

params.query:
UPDATE sync_ledger
SET status = 'synced', airtable_record_id = $2, quickbooks_invoice_id = $3, synced_at = now()
WHERE event_id = $1
RETURNING *;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [$('2 - Normalize and Validate Into One Standard Record').item.json.event_id, $('8 - Airtable: Create the Ops Project Record').item.json.id, $('9 - QuickBooks: Create the First Invoice').item.json.Id] }}

nodes.label: 14 - Any Node Fails, Anywhere
15 - Sync Ledger: Mark Failed, Ready to Replay

params.query:
UPDATE sync_ledger
SET status = 'failed', failed_step = $2, error = $3, failed_at = now()
WHERE execution_id = $1
RETURNING event_id, deal_id, failed_step, error;

nodes.label: 16 - Alert With the Deal, the Failed Step and a Run Link
